facts.raw_span: A 50-year-old man
known neurofibromatosis type 1
multiple cutaneous neurofibromas
no history of smoking
recurrent urinary retention and sepsis
transurethral resection of the prostate revealed fibroleiomyomatous hyperplasia
diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall without a discrete mass
bladder wall was diffusely thickened, firm, and gray–white, with near–complete loss of the detrusor muscle
diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix
dense, perivascular spindle cell proliferation with prominent cytological atypia, frequent mitoses, and an infiltrative growth pattern
tumor cells were positive for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56
tumor cells were negative for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin

concepts.why: The patient's known neurofibromatosis type 1 and the presence of a diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix, along with the tumor cells being positive for S100 and negative for various other markers, are consistent with a diagnosis of MPNST.

The patient's known neurofibromatosis type 1 and multiple cutaneous neurofibromas, along with the presence of a diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation, are consistent with a diagnosis of neurofibroma, although the presence of atypia and mitoses suggests a more malignant process.
The diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall and the diffusely thickened bladder wall with near-complete loss of the detrusor muscle are explained by this rare tumor type.

rationales.F02: Neurofibromatosis type 1 is associated with an increased risk of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors and neurofibromas.
rationales.F03: Multiple cutaneous neurofibromas are a common feature of neurofibromatosis type 1.
rationales.F09: The presence of a diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei and a collagenous matrix is suggestive of a neurofibroma or malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
rationales.F10: The presence of a dense, perivascular spindle cell proliferation with prominent cytological atypia, frequent mitoses, and an infiltrative growth pattern is highly suggestive of a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor.
rationales.F11: The tumor cells being positive for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56 is consistent with a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor or neurofibroma.
rationales.F12: The tumor cells being negative for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin helps to rule out other types of tumors.
